4 — The mark needs choices to hide in

annotations.text:
TRANSPOSING TO CANVA

Canvas: 1080 x 1350 (4:5 — tallest LinkedIn allows).
Margins: 84px all round.

Type
· Display: Archivo Black
· Body: Archivo (400 / 600)
Both in Canva.

Colours — AS PUBLISHED the deck runs on the alt-counsel purple, not the
white of these artboards. Purple fields: cover, 3, 6, 8. White fields:
2, 4, 5, 7. Reverse the type on the purple pages.
· Ink #000000
· Body grey #3A3A38
· Caption grey #6F6C66
· Keycap face #BBDDFF
· Keycap side #8AC0DD
· Pressed face #9B9A8F
· Pressed side #6F6C66
· Warm off-white #F4F3EF

Keycap = two rounded rects (radius 18, 4px black outline), darker one offset 18px down. A pressed key sits 14px lower than its neighbours.

THE RULE FOR THIS DECK: TEACH, DON'T ARGUE.

Under 35 words a page. No 'I think', no rebuttals, no qualifiers. If a page needs a paragraph, it's two pages.

The point lands by SEQUENCE, not by assertion: page 4 shows where the mark lives, page 5 shows the same picture in a contract, page 6 names why that matters. The reader draws the conclusion. The deck never states it.

If you add words back, add them to the caption, not the slides.

PAGES 2 AND 5 MUST MATCH EXACTLY.

Same keycap size, same spacing, same pressed key. Page 2 is harmless (the weather). Page 5 is a contract clause.

The whole deck turns on the reader recognising the second picture as the first. If you restyle the keys on one page, restyle both.
